title: Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is glitching out on this health metric, but a fix is on the way
summary: Track runners may not see VO2 Max data until Samsung fixes the issue.
body: TL;DR The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is facing issues showing VO2 Max data for “Track Running.” VO2 Max readings are working normally for other activities, including outdoor runs. Samsung has confirmed that it’s working on a fix and will roll it out with a future software update. If you’re using a Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 to log running sessions, you may have noticed it isn’t displaying VO2 Max data for certain running activities. Well, you’re not alone. It seems the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2’s VO2 Max calculations are failing for “track running” sessions despite good GPS coverage, pace, and activity time. According to a user report on the Samsung Community forums, the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is encountering an odd error when calculating VO2 Max. The user shared screenshots showing that their watch was not calculating or displaying VO2 Max readings after logging a track running session.

title: Xiaomi’s latest fitness tracker makes its way to more countries
summary: You can finally buy it without making a trip to China.
body: TL;DR The Xiaomi Smart Band 11 is now available in Europe. It’s slimmer at 9.99mm, weighs 15.58g without the band, and is available in both standard and NFC-equipped variants. The Xiaomi Smart Band 11 starts at around $67 in Europe for the standard, metal-cased version. Xiaomi launched its latest fitness tracker — the Xiaomi Smart Band 11 — in China early last month. However, although the band appeared on Xiaomi’s global website soon after, it only became available outside China earlier this month. Even then, it was only available in South Korea and Hong Kong. If you were waiting to snag one of Xiaomi’s super-sleek fitness bands without visiting China, you can now finally do so. The Xiaomi Smart Band 11 is now available in Europe and can be purchased in both standard and NFC-equipped variants. It’s priced at €59.99 (~$67) for the standard, non-NFC model, and €79.99 (~$89) for the Smart Band 11 with NFC.

title: Google’s Health Connect could support multiple user profiles on your device
summary: Multiple user profiles could soon be able to view and manage their data using Health Connect, all from one device.
body: TL;DR A future Android update may finally let multiple user profiles access Health Connect. Health Connect currently supports only one user, but code in the recent Android 17 QPR3 Beta 2 suggests that could change. If implemented, this would let multiple users manage app permissions and view or delete their existing health data, all from one device. Google Health Connect is a built-in Android tool that lets supported fitness and health apps read, write, and share data, while keeping it secure and on-device. Due to current limitations, Health Connect doesn’t support multiple user profiles, meaning its features aren’t available on other profiles. Thankfully, a future Android release could change that.
